svg.title: Wi-Fi Bridge for glider avionics
svg.desc: A small 3D-printed box in the glider collects data from Classic FLARM (traffic), the Zander ZS1 glider computer (flight data) and the Becker AR6201 radio, and sends it over Wi-Fi as NMEA over TCP to an app such as OpenSoar on a phone. The app can put an airfield frequency into the radio standby slot. Features: own Wi-Fi hotspot, status and settings page, data monitor, updates over Wi-Fi, 7 to 20 V supply, several apps at once, instrument presets, supply voltage monitor. Prototype in development.

g.text: Cockpit instruments to your phone or tablet, without a cable
The bridge: ESP32 in a 3D-printed box
